comments.author: @peterfillippsss
comments.text:
Hello again Epic Earth, so nice to receive your notification this morning. I see todays journey was a little different, in that i was taken to many places throughout the World to marvel at our creations. 
What a spectacular documentary you have put together show casing some truly remarkable engineering accomplishments. Well done. 
I often wonder what people from only a few centuries ago would think if they saw the World today. Such developmental progress has come in such a relatively short time period. And then, what would we think of the World if we were able to view it in a few more centuries with the rate of progression only getting faster and faster. 
I really liked the Bailong Elevator in China. Those natural stone pillars are mesmerising and the building seems to fit into the landscape without looking out of place. Also the Ya`an-Xichang Expressway in China is another standout. You used the word majestic to describe some of the bridges, that one word sums up this development perfectly. 
Thankyou again Epic Earth for all of your hard work in putting together these documentaries which allow me to visually travel the World each week and see and learn about different things and places. 
I hope you are keeping well and finding time for yourself. 
Kind regards😃

replies.author: @EpicEarthYTB
replies.text:
Hello my friend! Seeing your comment is always the warmest and most rewarding moment of my week! 😊

You noticed immediately that this episode was a little different—stepping back from raw, untouched wilderness to marvel at human audacity and engineering ingenuity. Your thought experiment about time gave me goosebumps: imagine someone from the 1700s standing at the base of the Bailong Elevator, watching glass ascend sheer sandstone pillars, or seeing the Ya'an-Xichang Expressway literally carved through the clouds above mountain gorges! It would look like pure sorcery to them. And you're completely right—with technological advancement accelerating exponentially, what humans will build in another few centuries is beyond our wildest imaginations today.

I'm so glad the Bailong Elevator and the Yaxi Expressway stood out to you. That balance where engineering respects the majesty of the landscape rather than destroying it is truly peak human craftsmanship.

Thank you so much for your kind reminder for me to take time for myself—creating these is intense work, so your care means the world to me. Please take wonderful care of yourself as well, rest up, and see you next week on our next journey! Warmest regards as always! 🏗️⛰️✨

comments.author: @EpicEarthYTB
comments.text: 🌍 Which is more extraordinary—the imagination to dream of the impossible or the ingenuity to make it real? Thank you for exploring these architectural wonders with us, and subscribe to Epic Earth for more incredible journeys.
